marble.name: Using Weather Instruments
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Use weather instruments to measure and record weather data: thermometers for temperature in °C, rain gauges for rainfall, wind vanes for direction, and anemometers for wind speed — and keep a weather diary over time
marble.prompt: If you had a thermometer, rain gauge, and wind vane at school, could they take daily readings, record them in a table, and spot patterns over a week or month?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering how weather works — learning about different types of weather, how to stay safe during storms, and understanding how weather patterns change with the seasons.

misconceptions: A wind vane measures wind SPEED — it shows DIRECTION; the anemometer measures speed
The rain gauge shows total rain ever — it is read then emptied for each period
Reading a thermometer from an angle gives the true value — must read at eye level
Any single reading describes the weather — patterns need repeated, consistent measurements over time
Bigger numbers are always 'more weather' — units and what is measured matter (mm of rain vs °C)
representations: An instrument panel pairing each tool with its quantity and unit
A weekly weather-diary table filling in day by day
A bar graph/pictograph built from the recorded data
A close-up scale (thermometer, rain gauge) for practising accurate reading
authoredAnswer: Reads the thermometer at eye level to the correct scale in °C, reads the rain gauge on a level surface at the meniscus, reads wind direction from the vane correctly (the arrow points to where the wind comes FROM), records each with date and units, and transfers the log into a correctly-scaled, labelled graph.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: eye not level with the liquid; misreads between graduations
wrongAnswers.fix: Model eye-level reading and reading to the nearest marked graduation.
The vane arrow points INTO the wind — name the direction it comes FROM.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: gauge not level, or resets it before recording
wrongAnswers.fix: Read on a flat surface at the meniscus; empty only AFTER recording.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: axis spacing inconsistent; no units on the scale
wrongAnswers.fix: Set equal intervals and label the axis with units before plotting.
